title: CARBON MONOXIDE DETECTOR - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the detailed procedures for removing and reinstalling the carbon monoxide detector in an aircraft with Garmin G1000 systems, including the steps to verify its proper operation after reinstallation?
answer:
WARNING: Inadequate panel replacement of the engine nacelle may compromise aircraft integrity. Always wear insulated gloves, follow approved methods, and check for discoloration before returning to service.

Carbon Monoxide Detector Removal . (1)  Put the AVIONICS MASTER switch in the off position. (2) Remove the MED from the copilot side of the instrument panel. Refer to Chapter 34, Control Display Unit - Maintenance Practices. (3) Disconnect the electrical connector  from the CO detector. (4) Remove and keep the three screws and three washers that connect the CO detector to the avionics support structure. (5) Remove the CO detector from the airplane.Carbon Monoxide Detector Installation . (1) Put the CO detector in position on the avionics support structure. (2) Attach the CO detector to the structure with the three kept screws and three kept washers. (3) Connect the electrical connector  to the CO detector. Install the MED on the copilot side of the instrument panel. Refer to Chapter 34, Control Display Put the AVIONICS MASTER switch in the ON position. (6) On the primary flight display , do a check to make sure that the CO detector operates AIRPLANES THAT HAVE GARMIN G1 000

title: CARBON MONOXIDE DETECTOR - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What should be checked before reapplying soundproofing and insulation materials after removal?
answer: The airplane utilizes soundproofing and insulation throughout the fuselage area. This material is glued into place using spray adhesive. Any time old material is being replaced, care should be taken to ensure all traces are removed from fuselage skin before reapplication. For a list of spray adhesives, refer to Equipment/Furnishing - General.For an illustration of soundproofing and insulation locations, refer to Figure 201 and Figure 202.

title: CARBON MONOXIDE DETECTOR - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What steps should be followed to properly remove and install the carbon monoxide detector in an aircraft equipped with Garmin G1000 systems?
answer:
WARNING: Inadequate panel replacement of the engine nacelle may compromise aircraft integrity. Always wear insulated gloves, follow approved methods, and check for discoloration before returning to service.

Carbon Monoxide Detector Removal . (1)  Put the AVIONICS MASTER switch in the off position. (2) Remove the MED from the copilot side of the instrument panel. Refer to Chapter 34, Control Display Unit - Maintenance Practices. (3) Disconnect the electrical connector  from the CO detector. (4) Remove and keep the three screws and three washers that connect the CO detector to the avionics support structure. (5) Remove the CO detector from the airplane.Carbon Monoxide Detector Installation . (1) Put the CO detector in position on the avionics support structure. (2) Attach the CO detector to the structure with the three kept screws and three kept washers. (3) Connect the electrical connector  to the CO detector. Install the MED on the copilot side of the instrument panel. Refer to Chapter 34, Control Display Put the AVIONICS MASTER switch in the ON position. (6) On the primary flight display , do a check to make sure that the CO detector operates AIRPLANES THAT HAVE GARMIN G1 000
